starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.text: Ho there, [player name]! Want to take a ride with me?

starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.player: Where are you going? Across the river?

starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.text: No no, that's what the ferryman is for! I'm going to Keldagrim, my home!

starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.player: How much will that cost me then?

starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
starting-off-talking-to-dwarven-boatman.text: For a human like you, I can do it for free!

steps.player: That's a deal!

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Excellent! I'm just waiting for my ship to arrive and then we can go.

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Mind, this trip could take a few minutes! Are you sure you're ready to go as well?

steps.player: Yes, I'm ready and don't mind it taking a few minutes.

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Well, let's not waste any more time then!
Note: The option to skip the cutscene only appears in Leagues and Community Event worlds.
Continues below at "Identify yourself, human!"

A cutscene starts. The screen displays the Keldagrim Palace. In large, red letters, "Keldagrim, Grand Capital of the Dwarven realm" appear on screen. The text disappears, and the following text appears next:

The camera pans throughout Keldagrim-West, and the text "Rise of the Red Axe Part 1" appears on screen. The camera then pans to the statue of King Alvis, and the text "The Giant Dwarf" appears. The scene then shifts to a map of the River Kelda, the statue, and a mini version of the dwarven boat, moving.

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Look, there's the statue of King Alvis, guarding the entrance to Keldagrim!

steps.player: Amazing! And we're going to go straight past it?

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: That's right!

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Er, hold on! There's something wrong!

steps.speaker: Both
steps.text: Aaargh!
The boat crashes into the statue, destroying it. The cutscene then shifts to the dock in Keldagrim. Two Black Guard Berserkers are seen standing on the dock

steps.speaker: Black Guard Berserker
steps.text: Halt!

steps.speaker: Black Guard Berserker
steps.text: Halt! By order of the Black Guard, you are under arrest!

steps.player: What?? I didn't do anything! It wasn't me!

steps.speaker: Black Guard Berserker
steps.text: Come with us, human! Commander Veldaban wants a word with you!
The cutscene ends, and the player arrives at the Black Guard Headquarters.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Identify yourself, human!

steps.player: I err, I'm [player name]. I was told I was under arrest. I had a little accident on the way in here.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Ah, so you're the one who knocked over the statue of our glorious king!

steps.player: I suppose so... I mean, I didn't do it on purpose or anything...

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Ah, don't worry about it!

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: We haven't been ruled by a king for many a year... that statue was long overdue for replacement anyway. You're not under arrest, I merely wanted to talk to you.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: But let me introduce myself. I am Veldaban, son of Dondakan. I am the Commander of the Black Guard in Keldagrim.
If the player has completed Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Dondakan, you say?
I helped your father in the mines south of the city.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Ah, so you are the one! I heard you banished a demon by defeating its avatar, most impressive.
If the player has started Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Dondakan, you say?
I'm helping your father in the mines south of the city.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Ah, he is forever trying to break open that rock of his, until his death I sometimes think.

steps.player: So you don't think it's possible?

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Perhaps, human, perhaps... but if even our multicannon does not dent it, what chance is there really?
If the player has not started Between a Rock...:

steps.player: Well, ehm... nice to meet you, Veldaban.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Now listen carefully. I have a task for you.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: I want you to go and see the local sculptor and help him build a new statue.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Will you do this for us?

steps.player: No, I can't be bothered.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: You destroy our statue and you cannot be bothered to help rebuild it? By Guthix, you are rude... even for a human!

steps.player: Yes, I will do this.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: You are a good human, [player name].

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Now, I need you to go to Blasidar, he is a sculptor who lives in Keldagrim-East.

steps.player: To be honest I'm not much of a sculptor myself.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: Oh, don't worry! I just need you to help him out while he rebuilds the statue.

steps.speaker: Commander Veldaban
steps.text: I'm sure there are many tasks that he needs doing.

steps.player: I'll see what I can do.
No, I don't have time right now, I'll be back later.

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Sure, sure! Come back when you need to!

options.text: I prefer the mines to the city.

steps.player: I prefer the mines to the city.

steps.speaker: Dwarven Boatman
steps.text: Well, suit yourself then!

starting-off-talking-to-veldaban-again-a.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-off-talking-to-veldaban-again-a.text: How are you getting on with rebuilding our statue, [player name]?

starting-off-talking-to-veldaban-again-a.player: I haven't really done much yet...

starting-off-talking-to-veldaban-again-a.speaker: Commander Veldaban
starting-off-talking-to-veldaban-again-a.text: Get back to it as soon as you can, please!

starting-off-talking-to-riki-before-agre.player: Hello there, can you help me?
What? No, I was wondering if you could help me.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.player: Excuse me, are you Blasidar, the famous sculptor?

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Why, yes, yes, that I am!

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.player: Oh, well, I'm [player name]. Veldaban of the Black Guard sent me to you, you see. Said you might need some help with the statue.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Oh, I don't need an assistant sculptor, really, I can do just fine on my own.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: And I've also got a model here, you see, to base my statue on.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: But come to think of it, I do need some errands run. Yes, quite important errands too.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Yes, you will do just fine.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.player: So what did you need doing?

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Well, see... the Consortium has commisioned me to rebuild the statue exactly the way it was.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: But the statue itself has broken into a million pieces... and we dwarves aren't very good painters, you know, so we don't have any paintings of it either.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.player: Not a very artistic race, then, are you?

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: No, that's not what I said, I said we're not very good painters.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: We're excellent with, for example, stone. Oh yes, quite good if I say so myself.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: But I digress... simply speaking, I need some help with getting some items that I can base the new statue on.

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Will you be able to help me with this, [player name]?

steps.player: No, I can't be bothered.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: How rude is that? I don't think the Black Guard will be very pleased with you!

steps.player: Yes, I will do this.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Excellent, excellent! Now what I need is the following...

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: I will need a pair of boots, the most exquisite boots you can find. The more they look like the original the better, but I don't think you'll be able to find an exact match.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: For the torso, I need clothes that look like King Alvis' clothes. I'm not sure where you would be able to find that, but I'm sure you'll manage.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Also, I need a battleaxe. Now this is particularly important. You are in luck, however, as I believe King Alvis' original axe still survives.

steps.player: Right, so I need a pair of boots, a piece of clothing and a battleaxe. Is that all?

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: For now, [player name], for now! I wish you good luck, and hurry back with the items!

steps.player: But... wait, wait, how am I supposed to find all this?

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: I don't know! You're supposed to find that out for me!

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: But it's a beautiful city, Keldagrim is, I'm sure you'll see many things while you do these tasks!

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.player: What was it you needed doing again?

starting-off-talking-to-blasidar-the-scu.text: Continues above from after "So what did you need doing?"

starting-off-talking-to-miodvetnir-derni.text: See Miodvetnir, Derni, and Dernu#Subsequent dialogue

clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-vermun.speaker: Vermundi
clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-vermun.text: Welcome to my clothes stall, can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, what clothes do you have in stock?
Yes, I'm looking for some special clothes.

steps.player: Yes, I'm looking for some special clothes.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh, that sounds interesting, what's this about?

steps.player: I'm helping the sculptor to rebuild the statue of King Alvis. But he wants to know what his clothes looked like.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh dear, that statue is in a terrible mess, isn't it?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I could hear the tumult from over here!

steps.player: But the clothes, do you have any similar clothes?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh no, no, I can't quite recall what the clothes looked like. But I know someone who can!

steps.player: Who's that?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Well, I'm sure Hugi the librarian in West can help you along.

steps.player: West?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Keldagrim-West, dear... on the other side of the Kelda, towards the north end of the city.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I'm sure he can show you the exact designs of the clothes.

steps.player: But I need the actual clothes themselves, not just the designs.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh, just bring the designs to me then, I'll fix you up some nice clothes!

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Sounds like a fun little thing to do!

steps.player: Great, thanks a lot, I'll check out the library!

clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-hugi.speaker: Librarian
clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-hugi.text: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the library?
Do you know anything about King Alvis' clothes?

steps.player: Do you know anything about King Alvis's clothes?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: His clothes? How do you mean?

steps.player: I'm helping Blasidar the sculptor to rebuild the statue of King Alvis, but he needs to know the design of his clothes.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I see, I see.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: There is a book, somewhere in the library, that may help you. It is the 'Scholars Guide to Dwarven Costumes' and it contains the designs of the costumes of a lot of old Kings and dwarven dignitaries.

steps.player: Sounds like just the thing. Where exactly could I find it?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: Let me think... I believe it is on the top shelf of one of the bookcases in the library, because it is such an old book.

steps.player: Can you be any more specific? Upstairs, downstairs?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I don't remember, sorry. You will have to try several bookcases. You will probably need the ladders, tall a human though you are.

steps.player: Well, thanks, I'll have a look.

steps.text: You have no reason to climb that very wobbly looking ladder.
As you put your foot on the bottom of the ladder, you hear it creak loudly... It nearly breaks! This ladder can't support your weight!

steps.player: Bah. Annoying dwarven ladders, they're much too flimsy.

steps.text: You dust off the book you just retrieved and read the title: 'Scholars Guide to Dwarven Costumes'. Just what you need! You can take this to the clothes stall in the palace market now.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-retrieving-the-bo.text: If you already have the book:

steps.text: You already have a copy of the 'Scholars Guide to Dwarven Costumes'. That's quite enough for you.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-retrieving-the-bo.text: You already have a copy of this book.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-returning-to-verm.speaker: Vermundi
clothes-fit-for-a-king-returning-to-verm.text: Welcome to my clothes stall, can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, what clothes do you have in stock?
Yes, about those special clothes again...

steps.player: Yes, about those special clothes again...

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh yes, did you get those designs from the librarian?
If the player has not spoken to Hugi:

steps.player: I haven't actually spoken to the librarian yet, let me do that now.

steps.text: If the player has spoken to Hugi but did not retrieve the book:

steps.player: No, I don't have them yet, but I can get them for you. The librarian has a book.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: A book, how wonderful!
If the player has the book on costumes:

steps.player: Yes, I have a book right here, have a look at it!

steps.text: The player gives the book to Vermundi.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Oh, I see, I see!

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I can definitely help you with this.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I only have one small problem, you see... I've run out of fuel for my spinning machine.

steps.player: What does it run on?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Steam, of course!

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: But I've used up all my coal and wood and I don't have the time to leave my stall to get them.

steps.player: Don't worry, I'll get them for you. Let's see... some coal and some logs. Shouldn't be too hard.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-lighting-the-spin.text: You bend down to light the logs.
If the player succeeds in lighting the logs.

steps.text: ...and successfully start the engine!

clothes-fit-for-a-king-lighting-the-spin.text: If the player fails to light the logs.

steps.text: ...but fail miserably.
Perhaps you should improve your firemaking skill? Or just try again...

clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-vermun.speaker: Vermundi
clothes-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-vermun.text: Welcome to my clothes stall, can I help you with anything?

options.text: Yes, what clothes do you have in stock?
Yes, about those special clothes again...

steps.player: Yes, about those special clothes again...

steps.text: If the player has not loaded the spinning machine:

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Well, like I said, I can't do anything really without my spinning machine.

steps.player: Right, and what did you need again to start the engine?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Some coal and logs should do it!
If the player has both items:

steps.player: I've got them right here!

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Then put them in the machine dear!
If the player has loaded the spinning machine but not started it:

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Well, the spinning machine is all ready now, except that it needs to be powered up.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: As soon as it's up and running, I can spin your clothes for you.

steps.player: How does that work?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Why, you light the logs of course!

steps.player: Okay, okay, I'll do it! Just a moment.

steps.text: If the player has started the engine on the spinning machine:

steps.player: Can I have those clothes now?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Yes, I can spin them for you, but I will have to ask you for a small payment of money for them.

steps.player: What, after all that work?

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I'm sorry, but the cloth to spin this is expensive. But for you, I can make the clothes for a nominal fee of 200 credits.

steps.player: I'll pay, I'll pay.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: Wonderful, let me get started then!
Vermundi spins the machine and makes the clothing.

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: There we go! And look how beautiful these clothes look!
exquisite clothes

steps.player: Thank you very much!
I won't pay, that's outrageous!

steps.speaker: Vermundi
steps.text: I'm sorry you feel that way, I was looking forward to making these clothes.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-attempting-to-pic.text: You're not sure what those clothes are for, but you don't need them. You have the clothes you need for the sculptor already.

clothes-fit-for-a-king-wearing-the-cloth.player: These clothes are too small for me, I might ruin them if I put them on. I'd better take them to the sculptor instead.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-saro.speaker: Saro
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-saro.text: Welcome to my store, human! Are you interested in buying anything?

options.text: Yes, I'm looking for some armour.
Yes, I'm looking for a pair of special boots.

steps.player: Yes, I'm looking for a pair of special boots.

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: Boots, you say? What kind of boots?

steps.player: The best you have! Boots fit for a king!

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: Hmm, let's see... Well, I've got this pair of very exclusive boots. They're not armoured, but they look nice.

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: Or rather, I had. I'm afraid I sold them, come to think of it.

steps.player: And you don't have anything else?

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: I don't normally stock boots, no, nothing that's appropriate for... what did you say? A king?

steps.player: Please, tell me! Who did you sell the boots to?

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: Old chap here in the west part of town, his name is Dromund. He's quite well known, not only for his wealth, but also for his... pecularities.

steps.player: What house does he live in?

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: Go out the door, and head north. You'll have the headquarters of the Black Guard on your left and the bank on your right. Keep heading north and you'll find Dromund's house on your right. Can't miss it!

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: And if you're going to try to get the boots off him, good luck. You'll need it.

steps.player: Thanks!

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-saro-aga.speaker: Saro
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-saro-aga.text: Welcome to my store, human! Are you interested in buying anything?

options.text: Yes, I'm looking for some armour.
Yes, I'm looking for a pair of special boots.

steps.player: Yes, I'm looking for a pair of special boots.

steps.speaker: Saro
steps.text: I thought I already told you where to get them?

steps.player: Oh yes. The old dwarf north of the bank has them, I remember now.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.player: Calm down! I just want to ask you a few questions.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: Are you with the Black Guard or something?

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: No, you wouldn't be, you're just a human.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: What do you want from me?

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.player: I went to the Quality Armour shop. The proprietor told me you have just recently purchased a pair of boots from him.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: Right, and nice they look too on my display tables.

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.player: You're not actually using them then? Might I be able to buy them off you?

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: They're mine and the last thing I'll do is part with them!

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.player: Tell me, how much will you accept for these boots?

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund.text: Get out you pesky human! The boots are mine and you're not having them!

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund-.player: Are you sure you don't want to give me those boots?

boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund-.speaker: Dromund
boots-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-dromund-.text: Get out of here before I get one of my servants to throw you out!

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-left-boo.text: If the player is in Dromund's line of sight:

steps.speaker: Dromund
steps.text: What are you doing there?!

steps.player: Nothing...

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-left-boo.text: If the player is outside Dromund's line of sight:

steps.text: left boot

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-right-bo.text: If the player is inside the house:

steps.speaker: Cat
steps.text: Get your hands off that, you dirty human!

steps.speaker: Dromund
steps.text: Stay away from there! Who do you think you are, coming into my house like that?
You don't think you'll be able to get close to this boot without the old dwarf noticing you, what with his cat guarding.

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-right-bo.text: If the player is inside the house and casts Telekinetic Grab on the boots, outside Dromund's line of sight:

steps.speaker: Dromund
steps.text: What are you doing, casting spells in my house? Get out!

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-right-bo.text: If the player is outside the house and casts Telekinetic Grab on the boots whilst it is in Dromund's line of sight:

steps.speaker: Dromund
steps.text: Hey! Is there someone at my window?

steps.speaker: Dromund
steps.text: Scram before I get the Black Guard to arrest you!

boots-fit-for-a-king-taking-the-right-bo.text: If the player is outside the house and casts Telekinetic Grab on the boots, whilst it is outside Dromund's line of sight:

steps.text: right boot

boots-fit-for-a-king-trying-to-pick-up-t.text: You already have the perfect pair of boots, you don't need to bother with this one.

boots-fit-for-a-king-wearing-the-boots.text: If the player only has one boot:

steps.player: What, wear just one boot? Besides, the boot is too precious for that.

boots-fit-for-a-king-wearing-the-boots.text: If the player has the left and right boot:

steps.text: You now have the perfect pair of boots to bring to the sculptor's model!
exquisite boots

boots-fit-for-a-king-wearing-the-boots.text: If the player has the exquisite boots:

steps.player: I shouldn't wear these boots, I don't want anything to happen to them before I bring them to the sculptor.

boots-fit-for-a-king-dropping-the-boots.text: You drop one boot, but then the other shoe falls... you've lost them both!

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.speaker: Santiri
an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.text: Welcome, human, to the Quality Weapons Shop! Can I interest you in a purchase?

options.text: Yes, I'm looking for some weapons.
Yes, I'm looking for a particular battleaxe.

steps.player: Yes, I'm looking for a particular battleaxe.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Fancy a particular colour then? Blue is quite popular at the moment, and red is on the rise.

steps.player: No, actually, I'm looking for King Alvis' axe.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: The King's axe!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: What would a human want with it?

steps.player: I've been tasked by Veldaban, Commander of the Black Guard in Keldagrim, to assist in every way possible with the rebuilding of King Alvis' statue.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Oh yes, the statue... a most unfortunate incident.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Not that I'm entirely sure that it was merely an accident, of course.

steps.player: How do you mean?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I'm not entirely sure what I mean, human. But the axe, you say, what exactly did you need it for?

options.text: Just give me the axe already, I know you have it!

steps.player: Just give me the axe already, I know you have it!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I'll give it to you, embedded into your head!

steps.player: I've had just about enough of this! Goodbye!

options.text: Blasidar the sculptor needs it for his statue.

steps.player: Blasidar the sculptor needs it for his statue. He wants a model for the axe, you see, and he believes the original axe still survives.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: And so it does!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: It's been in my family's care for a few generations now, after it has been lost for a long time.

steps.player: What happened to it?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I do not know how it got lost, but my great-grandfather found it at the banks of the Kelda, further downstream from the city.

steps.player: Can I see it?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: There is not much left of it, to be honest. The blade has almost completely rusted away, and the sapphires on the hilt were either stolen or were washed away by the river before it was found.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I doubt it is useful to Blasidar in this state, master sculptor though he is.

steps.player: Are you sure this is the real axe then?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Not entirely, no, but it matches the description well enough, and the holes for the sapphires are still clearly visible on the hilt. But since no one has a similar claim, I don't really care. It's genuine to me.

options.text: This is tedious, I've lost interest.

steps.player: This is tedious, I've lost interest.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I'll get back to work then.

options.text: Perhaps I can repair the axe?

steps.player: Perhaps I can repair the axe?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: On your own? I doubt it. The sapphires, perhaps, if you are a skilled enough crafter. But the blade...
If the player has a Smithing level between 1 and 29:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Your feeble smithing skills will be of no use. No, you will need expert help on this.
If the player has a Smithing level between 30 and 74:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: You're a decent smith, but this is far beyond your capabilities.
If the player has a Smithing level between 75 and 98:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Formidable though your smithing skills are, this is beyond your capabilities.
If the player has level 99 Smithing:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Clearly you are a master smith, perhaps one of the best human smiths in all of Gielinor. Yet this is beyond even you.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: What you need is the skills of an Imcando dwarf... but they must all be dead by now.
If the player has not completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.player: Perhaps I could try and find one?

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Yes, perhaps, perhaps...

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Perhaps the librarian, just due east of here, can help you.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Yes, I like the sound of this!
If the player has completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.player: Oh, I know where I can find an Imcando dwarf!
He actually made a sword for me a while ago. I'm sure I can get him to help me again.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Really? That is amazing news.

steps.player: He lives on a cliff at the very south end of Asgarnia, just south of Port Sarim. I can visit him again if you like.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Excellent! You can take a cart to Ice Mountain from the station here, that should help you get there faster.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I will entrust you with King Alvis' battleaxe, then, human.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Help to restore it to its former glory!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: And please ask Blasidar to return it to me after he's done with it, I would sure love to see the restored blade again.

steps.player: Thank you. I will not disappoint you.

options.text: I don't really care for it after all.

steps.player: I don't really care for it after all.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Then stop wasting my time.

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.speaker: Santiri
an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.text: Welcome, human, to the Quality Weapons Shop! Can I interest you in a purchase?

options.text: Yes, I'm looking for some weapons.
Yes, I'm looking for a particular battleaxe.

steps.player: Yes, I'm looking for a particular battleaxe.

steps.text: If the player still has the axe:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? You still have it, yes?

steps.player: Yes, but I was just wondering what I should be doing with this piece of junk.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Piece of junk??

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I thought you were going to put sapphires on it and bring it to an Imcando dwarf?

steps.player: Oh yes, of course, that's what I was going to do!

steps.text: If the player lost the axe:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? You still have it, yes?

steps.player: I... sort of... ehm...
Look, I lost it!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: At least you are honest, human.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: I found it, actually, after you lost it. I'm not happy with giving it to you again, but the rebuilding of the statue is important.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Be careful with it this time, alright?
If the player still has the axe and added sapphires to it:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? You still have it, yes?

steps.player: Yes, and I've crafted some sapphires on the hilt, look!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: That's a great start! Now if you can find an Imcando dwarf so the blade can be repaired, that would be even better!
If the player still has the axe and has had it restored by Thurgo:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? You still have it, yes?

steps.player: Yes, and I got Thurgo the Imcando dwarf to fix it up nice and proper! Look!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Oh, that's beautiful! All it needs now is three sapphires crafted onto the hilt.
If the player still has the axe and has fully restored it:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? You still have it, yes?

steps.player: Yes, and look, it's all fixed up now! I got Thurgo the Imcando dwarf to fix the blade, and I've crafted three sapphires onto the hilt.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: That is amazing! Absolutely astounding work!

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Go and give Blasidar a hand with it then, and make sure to tell him to send it back to me when he's done with it!
If the player has given the axe to Riki:

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: Ah, you mean King Alvis' axe? Didn't you give it to Blasidar?

steps.player: I did, actually, I was just wondering if he returned it to you yet.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: No, I believe he's still using it.

steps.speaker: Santiri
steps.text: But thanks for your help with restoring the axe to its former glory!

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.text: You already have King Alvis' axe. You're not sure what that axe is for, but you don't need it.

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-santiri.player: I should be very careful with this battleaxe, it's almost a museum piece! I don't want to damage it by wielding  it.

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-hugi-wi.speaker: Librarian
an-axe-fit-for-a-king-talking-to-hugi-wi.text: Welcome to the Keldagrim library, human traveller!

options.text: Can you tell me more about the library?
Can you help me find an Imcando dwarf?

steps.player: Can you help me find an Imcando dwarf?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: An Imcando dwarf, you say?

steps.player: Yes, I need the help of an Imcando dwarf to repair an ancient battleaxe.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I see, I see.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: Ah, I'm afraid I can't help you here, Keldagrim lost contact with that particular tribe of dwarves a long time ago.

steps.player: Is there no one else who can help me?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: I suppose you could try Reldo, in the palace of Varrock. He is a most capable human librarian and knows quite a bit about us dwarves.

steps.player: Do you think he can help me?

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: He lives quite a good deal closer to where the Imcando used to live than we do, so it is not unlikely. Tell him Hugi the librarian sent you and I'm sure he'll be happy to help.

steps.speaker: Librarian
steps.text: And take a cart to Ice Mountain from the station in the east side of the city. It'll help you get to Varrock faster.

options.text: What do you know about the Imcando dwarves?

steps.player: What do you know about the Imcando dwarves?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: The Imcando dwarves, you say? Let's see...

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Ah, yes... For many hundreds of years, they were the world's most skilled smiths. They used secret smithing knowledge passed down from generation to generation.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Unfortunately, about a century ago, the once thriving group was wiped out during the barbarian invasions of that time.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: I believe a few of them survived, but with the bulk of their population destroyed, their numbers dwindled even further. If any are left now, they'll no doubt keep to themselves.

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: However, I have heard tales of their love for redberry pie. Perhaps one of those could convince one to reveal their true heritage.

steps.player: So I just go around offering random dwarves redberry pie?

steps.speaker: Reldo
steps.text: Well, not totally random. Apparently some of the surviving Imcando made a home for themselves near the cliffs on the Asgarnian southern peninsula. That would be a good place to start.

options.text: Can you help me with this ancient axe?

steps.player: Can you help me with this ancient axe?

steps.text: If the player has not completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: No. I don't do that anymore. I'm getting old.

options.text: Would you like a redberry pie?
options.condition: If you have a redberry pie in your inventory:

steps.text: If the player has completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Well, you know what to do! Get me another redberry pie and I'll have a look at that axe of yours!

options.text: Would you like a redberry pie?
options.condition: If you have a redberry pie in your inventory:

options.text: Would you like a redberry pie?
options.condition: If you have a redberry pie in your inventory:

steps.player: Would you like a redberry pie?

steps.text: You see Thurgo's eyes light up.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: I'd never say no to a redberry pie! We Imcando dwarves love them - they're GREAT!
You hand over the pie. Thurgo eats the pie. Thurgo pats his stomach.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: By Guthix! THAT was good pie! Anyone who makes pie like THAT has got to be alright!

options.text: Can you help me with this ancient axe?

steps.player: Can you help me with this ancient axe?

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: You make excellent redberry pies, [player name], so how can I refuse? Let me see what's wrong with it then.

steps.player: Here... the blade of this axe has become extremely dull and brittle. I need it restored to its former glory.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Its former glory eh? May I ask where exactly you got this axe from?

steps.player: It was given to me by someone in Keldagrim. I prefer not to say any more than that.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Ah, Keldagrim. We have not been there for a long time.

steps.player: We?

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Hand me the axe and I'll fix it right up for you.
If the player has not completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.player: Will you need any materials?

steps.text: If the player has completed The Knight's Sword:

steps.player: You don't want any blurite this time?

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Oh no, blurite is not appropriate here. No no, this is going to be a very delicate piece of work, requiring only a small amount in the way of raw materials.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Can you get me one bar of iron? Then I'll be able to start my work on this.
If the player does not have an iron bar:

steps.player: Of course.

steps.text: If the player has an iron bar:

steps.player: I've got one right here.

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Good, good! Hand me the axe and I'll get to work.
The screen fades to black briefly.
If the sapphires haven't been added yet:

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Here's your axe, [player name]. It looks like there's some damage to the hilt as well, probably some missing sapphires. But I'm sure you can take care of that yourself.
If the sapphires were already added:

steps.speaker: Thurgo
steps.text: Here you go, [player name], good as new.

steps.player: Thanks for your help Thurgo!

steps.text: If the sapphires haven't been added yet:
You are well on your way to restoring the axe. Do you wish to return to Keldagrim now?
If the sapphires were already added:
You have restored the axe to its former glory! You should return to Blasidar in Keldagrim now, do you wish to return at once?
The screen fades to black briefly, and the player arrives at Keldagrim, where Blasidar is.

options.text: What is that cape you're wearing?
What is that cape you're wearing?

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-using-sapphires-on.text: You take three of your cut sapphires and start your work...
Great, all it needs now is a little sharpening!

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-using-the-sapphire.text: Excellent, you've restored the battleaxe to its former glory! You'd better bring it to Blasidar the sculptor now.

an-axe-fit-for-a-king-trying-to-wield-th.text: I went through all this trouble to restore this axe, I'm not going to ruin it now by wielding it and accidentally smashing it to pieces. I'd better take it to the sculptor.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: How are you getting along with those items, [player name]?
If the player has not finished getting boots:

steps.player: I don't have your boots yet.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: If the player has exquisite boots in their inventory:

steps.player: I have your boots!

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Excellent, excellent! Go and give them to Riki over there so I can start my work on the base of the statue!

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: What else?
If the player has the boots but not finished getting clothes:

steps.player: I don't have your clothes yet.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: If the player doesn't have the boots or clothes:

steps.player: I also don't have your clothes yet, I'm afraid.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: If the player has exquisite clothes in their inventory:

steps.player: I had Vermundi make these clothes!

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Oh yes, Vermundi is a good woman, she's very reliable. Wonderful clothing. Give it to Riki please.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: And? The battleaxe?
If the player has not finished getting the battleaxe:

steps.player: Sorry, no, I'm still looking for it.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Look a little harder please!

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: If the player has a dwarven battleaxe in their inventory, but hasn't fully restored it:

steps.player: Look, I've got it right here.

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: What, that old thing? Is that a piece of rubbish you found in the garbage?

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: It looks so brittle it might well fall apart at any moment. I can't base my statue on that!

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Besides, from what I recall of the original axe, this doesn't even look anything like it.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: If the player has a fully restored dwarven battleaxe in their inventory:

steps.player: Oh, yes, I've got it right here!

steps.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
steps.text: Good job! Riki is your man, right over there. Give it to him please!

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-riki-the-.player: Don't worry, I'll be back later with all those items!
Don't worry, I'll be back with the rest of the items later!
I'll be back with the last item before you know it!
I have some clothes for you to wear.
I have this battleaxe for you.
Here, I have these boots for you to wear.
And look, I have some clothes as well!
And finally, I have this battleaxe for you!
Hey, you're looking nice in that outfit!
So is the job done now?
Care to tell me why not?
It's very tiring trying to talk to you, you know?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: I've all the items you asked me to get you. Can you make the statue now?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Yes, yes, that will do just fine. There is only one problem now, I still need to make the head.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: So you need me to find a crown now as well?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Oh no, no no, apparantly the Consortium has decided that crowns are out of fashion. As well as kings. Well, kings have been out of fashion here for hundreds of years.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: So what is the head supposed to look like now?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: I don't think they've quite made a decision on that. You see, I think each of the directors of the Consortium fancies their own face on top of the statue.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: What? But I thought the whole point was that it would look like king what's-his-face?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Yes, the Consortium can be a little fickle like that, unfortunately.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: But can you go and see if they've made a decision yet? I can't very well continue working on this statue without knowing what the face should look like, can I?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: No, I suppose you can't. Alright, I'll check it out.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Great! In the mean time, I'll build the statue up to the neck!
The screen fades to black, and the partially completed statue is shown. The screen then fades and returns to the player.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Any word from the Consortium yet?

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.player: No, the directors have not made a decision yet.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.speaker: Blasidar the sculptor
the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-blasidar-.text: Then please, try to persuade one of the directors to force the Consortium into a decision. I must finish this statue before I can move onto my other work.

the-head-of-a-dwarf-talking-to-riki-the-.player: I'm glad I don't have to talk to you anymore!
